children: Jefferies gives several reasons for upgrading engineering contractor NRW Holdings to buy, from hold. Contract wins have blunted risk around what a transition year for NRW. Investors had been worried about the impact of contractual work at Northern Star's Fimiston project ending. NRW's share price has fallen around 17% since the start of October. Analyst John Campbell says the stock's underperformance reflects the global AI rout and concerns around data centers. There's uncertainty over how this could affect the work pipeline for NRW's Fredon business. "Our two Perth trips this year however have materially bolstered our confidence around the underpinnings and duration of this resource capex (and exploration) cycle," Jefferies says. "The transition year issue is largely priced in and de-risked while the FY28 outlook is strengthening." (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
